title: How long does it take to learn After Effects well enough for a brand video?
meta_title: How Long to Learn After Effects? — Akdeinz Motion
description: Learning After Effects well enough for a brand video takes an estimated 55–110 hours. See the stages, the cost of your time and the €390 alternative.
answer: Starting from zero, expect roughly 55–110 hours of practice before After Effects work looks good enough for a brand video, which is about 11–22 weeks at 5 hours a week. If your time is worth more than the price, hiring is cheaper: a Logo Sting is €390 in 3 working days and a Brand Film is €2,400 in 10–14 working days, excl. VAT.

diy.intro: After Effects is the standard tool for motion design, and it can do almost anything. The cost is the learning curve. The hours below are estimates for a person with no animation background who practises on real projects.

tools.name: After Effects
tools.note: Industry standard timeline and compositing tool. Paid Adobe subscription.

tools.name: Jitter
tools.note: A lighter, browser-based route to simple brand animations while you decide whether to commit to After Effects.

tools.name: CapCut and Canva
tools.note: Faster for simple posts, but they do not replace After Effects skills for custom brand work.

steps: Basics (about 10–20 hours): interface, compositions, layers, keyframes, easing and the graph editor.
Shapes, text and masks (about 15–30 hours): building logo reveals, lower thirds and animated text from scratch.
Structure and speed (about 20–40 hours): pre-compositions, parenting, simple expressions and reusable templates.
Sound, export and polish (about 10–20 hours): syncing to audio, motion principles, exporting for different ratios and platforms.
diy.hours: Adding the stages gives roughly 55–110 hours. At 5 hours a week that is 11–22 weeks. Each extra aspect ratio and each revision then takes more of your time.

p: Multiply the hours by your own hourly rate. As an example only, at €50/hour, 55–110 hours is €2,750–€5,500 of your time, before the software subscription.
For comparison, a Brand Film of up to 60 seconds with Akdeinz Motion is €2,400 excl. VAT, delivered in 10–14 working days, and a Logo Sting is €390 in 3 working days.

diy_fine.p: Learning After Effects yourself makes sense when:
ul: You want motion design as a skill or a career, not only one video.
You will make a steady stream of videos for years, so the learning cost is spread out.
You enjoy the craft and have the weeks to spend.
Your needs are small and a lighter tool such as Jitter would do.
diy_fine.not_fine: If you need one or a few videos, or a steady monthly flow without learning a tool, a retainer is the middle route: Motion Monthly 8 is 8 × Social Motion Ad S for €2,890 per month (3-month minimum).

faq.q: Can I learn After Effects in a month?
faq.a: You can learn the basics in a few weeks, but reaching brand-video quality usually takes longer. Our estimate is 55–110 hours of practice.

faq.q: Is After Effects worth learning for a small business?
faq.a: Only if you will make videos regularly or want the skill. For one or a few videos, the hours usually cost more than hiring.

faq.q: What is an easier tool than After Effects?
faq.a: Jitter, Canva and CapCut are easier to learn but give less control.

faq.q: How much does it cost to hire instead?
faq.a: A Logo Sting is €390 (3 working days), a Social Motion Ad S is €490 (3–4 working days), and a Brand Film is €2,400 (10–14 working days). Prices are excl. VAT.

faq.q: Do I get the After Effects project file?
faq.a: No. The deliverable is the rendered video file only.
